classification.rationale: Adversarial architecture research and implementation revisions resolved demonstrated telemetry reliability uncertainties without making a legal or tax determination.

rd.researchQuestion: Can ROS preserve provider-neutral execution evidence correctly under concurrent local callbacks and bounded repository storage without adopting a new database or journal?
rd.hypothesis: Atomic replacement, resource-scoped locks, bounded raw/history retention, and explicit validation invariants are sufficient at demonstrated local scale.
rd.technicalUncertainty: The first implementation had not tested concurrent read-modify-write, crash-visible cross-file gaps, delayed provider timestamps, high-volume retention, or overlapping execution timing.
rd.experimentalObjective: Attempt to falsify the execution-envelope architecture through concurrent starts, concurrent ingestion/finalization, provider capability changes, retention exhaustion, and structural tampering.
alternativesEvaluated: append-only event journal with materialized execution views
rd.resultingTechnicalKnowledge: The current envelope can support demonstrated local concurrency with bounded sensitive payloads; append-only or distributed persistence is not yet justified without scale or cross-host evidence.
discoveredLimitations: cross-file creation and backlinking are validated but not transactionally atomic
whole-record writes remain costly at extreme callback volume
local locks do not coordinate independent hosts or network filesystems
rd.followUpExperiment: Profile version-pinned live provider runs and reopen storage when retention, size, or lock-contention thresholds are observed.
